name: waydroid-mcp

tools.name: status
tools.description: Waydroid's state: session and container, adb serial, whether Android has booted, Android and LineageOS versions, graphics, the per-app window service and the apps open in it, and how root access is set up. Call this first.

tools.name: session
tools.description: Starts, stops or restarts the Waydroid session. `start` waits until Android has booted (about 20-30 s). Stopping closes every Android app.

timeout_s.description: How long `start` waits for Android to boot.

tools.name: list_displays
tools.description: Android's displays with id, name, size and density, plus the apps open in their own windows or hidden displays. Display 0 is Waydroid's main window; input and screenshots take a display id or a package.

tools.name: root_access
tools.description: Sets up root in Android for `shell` with root and `stack_dump`. adb root is disabled in Waydroid, so root runs `sudo waydroid shell`. Pass a file holding the sudo password, or nothing to use sudo without one (a NOPASSWD rule). With check, runs `id -u` as root once; if sudo rejects the password, root stays off so repeated failures can't lock sudo.

password_file.description: Absolute path of a file containing the sudo password.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: Installed Android packages with their names. `launchable` lists apps with a launcher icon, including system apps such as Settings.

filter.description: Case-insensitive text to match in the package or app name.

tools.name: app_info
tools.description: One package's version, SDK levels, debuggable flag, paths, launcher activity, running processes, open display and permissions.

tools.name: launch_app
tools.description: Opens an app. `window` opens it in its own desktop window and `hidden` on an off-screen display with no window (both need waydroid-app-displays; hidden defaults to 1080x2340 at 440 dpi). `waydroid` uses Waydroid's own window. `size` fixes the Android display in pixels and `dpi` its density (dp width = pixels * 160 / dpi), so 720x1280 at 320 dpi is a 360 dp phone. Launching an open app again applies the new options, and options left out go back to the defaults. Returns the display id that input, screenshot and ui_tree act on; it changes each time the app is closed and opened.

mode.description: Default: window when the waydroid-app-displays service is running, otherwise waydroid.

size.description: Android display size WIDTHxHEIGHT in pixels, such as 1080x2340.

restart.description: Force-stop the app first, for a cold start.

tools.name: start_activity
tools.description: Starts an activity with an intent on a display, and waits for it to draw: open a URL or deep link (`url`), or an exact component such as com.android.settings/.Settings. Returns `am start -W`'s timing (TotalTime is the launch time in ms).

package.description: App to act on. An app in its own window or hidden display is found by package; otherwise Waydroid's main display is used.

display_id.description: Android display id instead of a package; 0 is Waydroid's main display.

url.description: Data URI for an ACTION_VIEW intent, such as https://example.com or myapp://path.

action.description: Intent action. Default: android.intent.action.VIEW with url, otherwise MAIN.

tools.name: install_apk
tools.description: Installs an APK, or a split bundle (.apks, .xapk, .apkm), from a host path or an http(s) URL. Replaces an installed version by default. Returns the package name and version.

source.description: Host path or URL of the APK or bundle.

extra_splits.description: More split APK paths installed together with source.

allow_test.description: Allow test-only APKs, as Android Studio debug builds are (-t).

tools.name: app_action
tools.description: Changes an app's state: force_stop, clear_data (also stops it), uninstall, uninstall_keep_data, grant or revoke a runtime permission, or close_window (closes its own window or hidden display; the app keeps running).

permission.description: For grant and revoke, such as android.permission.CAMERA.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Screenshot of an app's display or of Waydroid's main display, returned as an image and saved as a full-resolution PNG. Tap coordinates are display pixels: when the image is scaled down, divide image coordinates by the scale it reports.

package.description: App to act on. An app in its own window or hidden display is found by package; otherwise Waydroid's main display is used.

display_id.description: Android display id instead of a package; 0 is Waydroid's main display.

max_size.description: Longest side of the returned image in pixels; 0 returns full size.

wait_ms.description: Wait this long first, for a page change or animation after input.

tools.name: record_screen
tools.description: Records a display to an MP4 file on the host for a fixed time, then returns its path.

package.description: App to act on. An app in its own window or hidden display is found by package; otherwise Waydroid's main display is used.

display_id.description: Android display id instead of a package; 0 is Waydroid's main display.

tools.name: ui_tree
tools.description: The accessibility tree of the windows on an app's display: one line per element with class, text, hint, description, #resource-id, state flags, @center coordinates to tap and bounds, all in display pixels. Works on hidden and unfocused displays. Hides layout-only and off-screen elements unless all_nodes.

package.description: App to act on. An app in its own window or hidden display is found by package; otherwise Waydroid's main display is used.

display_id.description: Android display id instead of a package; 0 is Waydroid's main display.

tools.name: input
tools.description: Touch and keyboard input on a display, in display pixels. tap and long_press take x and y, or `element`: text, description or resource id to find in the UI tree. swipe goes from x,y to x2,y2 (swipe up to scroll down). text types into the focused field, so tap the field first; key sends a key such as BACK, ENTER, TAB, HOME or DEL.

package.description: App to act on. An app in its own window or hidden display is found by package; otherwise Waydroid's main display is used.

display_id.description: Android display id instead of a package; 0 is Waydroid's main display.

element.description: For tap and long_press: element text, content description or resource id.

duration_ms.description: Swipe or long-press length. Defaults: 300 and 800.

tools.name: logcat
tools.description: Recent Android log lines, filtered by app, tag, priority, time and regex. Android's clock is UTC. For logs that keep coming, such as while you reproduce a bug, use logcat_follow.

package.description: Only lines logged by this app's uid. System apps such as Settings share uid 1000 with system_server.

tags.description: logcat filter specs such as "ActivityManager:I" or "chromium:V"; tags not listed are hidden.

min_priority.description: Lowest priority shown, for every tag not in tags.

grep.description: JavaScript regular expression a line must match.

since_s.description: Only lines from the last N seconds.

lines.description: Return at most the last N matching lines.

tools.name: logcat_follow
tools.description: Follows the Android log in the background across calls. `start` begins collecting new lines with the same filters as logcat and returns an id. `read` returns the lines since the last read; with wait_for it first waits up to timeout_s for a line matching that regex, such as a crash (FATAL EXCEPTION) or your own log message. `stop` ends it; `list` shows all.

id.description: Follower id for read and stop.

package.description: Only lines logged by this app's uid. System apps such as Settings share uid 1000 with system_server.

tags.description: logcat filter specs such as "ActivityManager:I" or "chromium:V"; tags not listed are hidden.

min_priority.description: Lowest priority shown, for every tag not in tags.

grep.description: JavaScript regular expression a line must match.

wait_for.description: For read: regex to wait for in new lines.

timeout_s.description: For read with wait_for: the longest wait.

max_lines.description: For read: return at most the last N new lines.

tools.name: crashes
tools.description: Lists recent Java crashes and native crashes and ANRs, newest first, from Android's dropbox (kept across reboots), tombstones and ANR traces, optionally for one app. Pass `read` with an id from the list for the full report and stack.

package.description: Only crashes of this process or package.

since_h.description: How many hours back to look.

read.description: An id from the list, such as tombstone:tombstone_03, to return that report.

tools.name: stack_dump
tools.description: Thread stacks of a running app without killing it: Java stacks (`java`), native backtraces (`native`), or both. Uses debuggerd as root (see root_access). Useful for a frozen app or an ANR in progress.

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Records a Perfetto system trace (scheduling, frames, binder, app trace sections) for duration_s and saves it on the host. With package, the app's own Trace sections are recorded; with launch, the app is force-stopped and launched a second into the trace to capture a cold start. Open the file at https://ui.perfetto.dev.

categories.description: atrace categories. Default: sched freq idle gfx view wm am input binder_driver dalvik hal res.

tools.name: app_perf
tools.description: An app's memory (PSS summary from meminfo), frame rendering stats (jank percentage and frame time percentiles from gfxinfo) and CPU use. reset_frames clears the frame stats afterwards, so the next call measures only what happens in between.

tools.name: props
tools.description: Android system properties. `waydroid` lists Waydroid's persist.waydroid.* settings with their meaning and current value. `get` reads names or a regex. `set` changes one: persist.waydroid.* through `waydroid prop set`, others with setprop (debug.*, log.tag.* and persist.log.tag.* work without root). Most Waydroid settings apply after a session restart.

pattern.description: For get: regex matched against every property name.

value.description: For set; an empty string clears the property.

tools.name: shell
tools.description: Runs a shell command in Android and returns its output and exit code: dumpsys, am, pm, cmd, wm, getprop and so on. Runs as adb's shell user, or as root with root: true (see root_access). Nothing can be piped into it.

tools.name: files
tools.description: Copies files between the host and Android: push a host path to an Android path, or pull an Android path to the host. App-private files under /data/data are readable with pull only for debuggable apps (through run-as), given `package`.

package.description: For pull from a debuggable app's private directory.

tools.name: ports
tools.description: Connects ports between the host and Android over adb. `reverse` makes a host server reachable from Android (reverse tcp:8000 tcp:8000, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in Android). `forward` makes an Android socket reachable from the host. `devtools` forwards a Chromium-based browser's DevTools to a host port and lists its pages. `remove` undoes one, `list` shows all.

android.description: Android side, such as tcp:8000 or localabstract:chrome_devtools_remote.

tools.name: host_logs
tools.description: Host-side logs of Waydroid: `waydroid` is /var/lib/waydroid/waydroid.log (container start, mounts, errors), `container` the waydroid-container service's journal, `session` the session's journal, and `kernel` the kernel log (binder, GPU and overlay errors).

since.description: For journal sources: journalctl --since, such as "10 min ago".

instructions: Tools to run, drive and debug Android apps in Waydroid on a Linux desktop. Call `status` first; `session` starts Waydroid if it's stopped. Open apps with `launch_app`: `hidden` runs an app on an off-screen display at a chosen size and density, which suits automated checks. Act on an app by package name; input coordinates are display pixels. Debug with `logcat`, `logcat_follow`, `crashes`, `stack_dump`, `trace` and `app_perf`. Files the tools write (screenshots, recordings, traces) go to /tmp/waydroid-mcp.
